paper.title: An Experimental Design for Anytime-Valid Causal Inference on Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Mixture Adaptive Design: anytime-valid design-based ATE inference in two-armed bandit experiments
unmapped: design-based (finite-population) model: potential outcomes are fixed, non-random; randomness only from treatment assignment
goal is an anytime-valid asymptotic confidence sequence for the running average treatment effect, not regret minimization
potential outcomes eventually bounded by an unknown constant M (limsup |Y_t(w)| <= M)
the design mixes an arbitrary bandit algorithm with a Bernoulli design with weight delta_t
settings.definition_quote: For any treatment assignment algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ and a real-valued sequence $\delta_i \in (0, 1]$, ... $p^{\text{MAD}}_{t}(w) = \delta_t (1/2)+ (1-\delta_t)p_{t}^{\mathcal{A}}(w)$. ... Our objective is to generate a confidence sequence for $\bar{\tau}_t$ in MAB experiments with anytime-valid Type I error control.

symbols.S_hat: sum over i<=t of estimated variance bounds sigma_hat_i^2

conditions: Assumption 2: cumulative conditional variances of the IPW estimator grow at least linearly, Omega(t)

source.label: thrm1
source.quote: Then, under Assumptions~\ref{a_bound} and~\ref{a_var2} and setting $\delta_t = \omega\left(\frac{1}{t^{1/4}}\right)$, $(\hat{\bar{{\tau}}}_{t} \pm \hat{V}_t)$ is a valid $(1-\alpha)$ asymptotic CS for $\bar{\tau}_t$ and $\hat{V}_t \stackrel{a.s.}{\to} 0$.

results.notes: Not a regret bound: the guarantee is that the half-width V_hat_t yields an asymptotically valid (1-alpha) confidence sequence for the running ATE and V_hat_t -> 0 a.s. The expression recorded is the CS half-width. The analogous statements for K arms (Theorem 1*) and batched designs (Theorem 1†) are in the appendix.

conditions: running ATE converges to a nonzero constant c

source.label: thrm2
source.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem \ref{thrm1}, if $\bar{\tau}_t \to c$ for some $|c| > 0$ as $t \to \infty$, then $$\mathbb{P}\left(T_{MAD} < \infty\right) = 1.$$

results.notes: The expression is the probability that the stopping time (first time the CS excludes 0) is finite. Theorem 3 gives the same for the underlying exact CS, and Lemma 3.1 gives it for the Howard et al. CS. K-arm and batched versions are in the appendix.
